extraction.name: AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes
extraction.description: AMASS is a large database of human motion that unifies 15 optical marker-based motion capture datasets within a common framework and parameterization. It represents motions as SMPL body model parameters and provides fully rigged 3D human meshes with pose, shape, soft-tissue motion, and hand articulation. The dataset contains 42 hours of mocap data from 346 subjects and 11,451 motions.
extraction.creator: Naureen Mahmood (Meshcapade GmbH); Nima Ghorbani (MPI for Intelligent Systems); Nikolaus F. Troje (York University); Gerard Pons-Moll (MPI for Informatics); Michael J. Black (MPI for Intelligent Systems)
extraction.citeAs: Naureen Mahmood, Nima Ghorbani, Nikolaus F. Troje, Gerard Pons-Moll, and Michael J. Black. AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes. arXiv:1904.03278v1, 2019.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: AMASS was assembled by unifying 15 existing optical marker-based motion capture datasets into a common format using MoSh++; the publicly available datasets were downloaded from the internet, several others were obtained privately, some were recorded by the authors themselves, and the SSM dataset was newly collected using a synchronized optical motion capture and 4D body scanning setup.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis; Manual Human Curator; Physical data collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: During mocap sessions, markers may get occluded by the body due to pose; the paper also notes inherent mocap problems such as swapped and mislabeled markers, which were manually inspected and either corrected or held out.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data consisted of archival optical marker-based human motion capture recordings from 15 source datasets with varying marker sets, and for SSM, synchronized mocap marker data and high-resolution 4D body scans captured with an OptiTrack motion capture system and a 3dMD 4D body scanning system.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: MoSh++ was used to map marker-based motion capture data into common SMPL pose, shape, and soft-tissue parameters; due to problems with mocap such as swapped and mislabeled markers, the authors manually inspected the results and either corrected or held out problems.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: MoSh++ was used to map marker data into SMPL pose, shape, and soft-tissue parameters, after which the authors manually inspected the results and either corrected or held out problems caused by issues such as swapped and mislabeled markers.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Current runtime for MoSh++ is not real-time; We do not have ground-truth data for evaluating accuracy of hand articulation
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: We provide the largest unified mocap dataset (AMASS) to the community, enabling new applications that require large amounts of training data
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset consists of three subjects with varying body shapes, performing a total of 30 different motions. Two of the three subjects were professional models who signed modeling contracts; this allows us to release their 4D scan data, along with the synchronized mocap data for the research community.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: applications in animation and computer vision; animation, visualization, and generating training data for deep learning; generating synthetic training for computer vision tasks
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: With MoSh++ it is easy to add more data and we will continue to expand the dataset; We will continuously incorporate more mocap data contributed by us and the community
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: We separate the sequences into training and testing sets, and train the hyperparameters of MoSh++ to minimize the distance between the ground truth 3D scans and the estimated 3D body meshes. We separated 20% of the total captured mocap files from the three subjects as a held-out set for testing and evaluation. The first 200 frames of the rest of the motion files are used for training, leaving the remaining frames (roughly 60% of the training set) for validation.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Due to inherent problems with mocap, such as swapped and mislabeled markers, we manually inspected the results and either corrected or held out problems.
